newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche to revamp branch network.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche to revamp branch network.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest commercial bank, said on Wednesday it would reorganise its network of regional branches to become more competitive.
The bank said in a statement that it had divided up its business in Germany into eight regions and would set up three new main branches in Rostock, Dresden and Nuremburg.

Deutsche at present has 18 main branches which act as regional headquarters, overseeing the bank's business in their respective areas. The bank said it did not plan to reduce the number of its retail branches as part of the reorganisation.
The bank had 1,652 branches in Germany at the end of September.
"Deutsche Bank is reorganising its branch structure to increase its competitiveness further," the bank said.
"It wants to get closer to customers, boost its capacity for decentralised decision-making and improve the quality of service."

The bank said its west German branch network was adopting the regional structure it had set up for its business in east Germany after unification, where it has two regions with main branches in Berlin and Leipzig.
A spokesman for the bank said administrative tasks like accounting would be combined within each region. It will have six regions in western Germany and two in eastern Germany.
